title: Rachmaninoff and Richter: the Adagio opening
work: Piano Concerto No. 2, Op. 18 — II. Adagio sostenuto, opening-side comparison only
question: How do Rachmaninoff and Richter connect the Adagio’s long phrases with the piano’s smaller moving notes?
intro: Rachmaninoff, Stokowski and the Philadelphia Orchestra recorded the Adagio’s first side on 10 April 1929; Richter’s reference recording with Wisłocki and the Warsaw National Philharmonic Orchestra dates from 1959. Only HMV D.B. 1334’s Adagio opening is used, matching 0–214.4 seconds of Richter to 3–174 seconds of the historical transfer and excluding the later cadenza and return. The provisional map has median chroma confidence 0.854 after shifting the historical pitch-class features down one semitone, without altering the audio. Surface noise weakens some local matches, so these passages invite comparison of broad phrasing rather than beat-exact rubato or speed-corrected historical tempo.
